counterevidence_considered.description: The raw input does contain eight correlated rows per colony (80 rows for 10 colonies), so the ingredient for the issue class is present in the data; if the paired t-test had been applied to trial rows directly, the same colony would have entered the row-independent procedure repeatedly. This is the strongest point in favor of the issue, but the workflow demonstrably aggregates before testing, so the hazard is not realized.
counterevidence_considered.observed_value: 80 trial rows = 10 colonies x 2 conditions x 4 trials per condition

source_refs.quoted_text: The input table `data/input.csv` holds 80 trial rows: 10 colonies x 2 conditions x 4 trials per condition.

counterevidence_considered.description: Session-level structure (sessions 1-4 within a colony) is averaged over rather than modeled, and site and block order are tabulated but not included in the test; one could argue some structure is ignored. However, averaging over within-unit structure is the aggregation the data description itself prescribes, and the report acknowledges the site/colony confound, so this does not constitute repeated entry of an independent unit into a row-independent procedure.
counterevidence_considered.observed_value: site and block_order reported descriptively only; site confound acknowledged

source_refs.quoted_text: Every colony (10 of 10) foraged less under the warmed setting; the smallest colony-level drop was 0.70 and the largest 4.60 sorties per hour. The confidence interval excludes zero, so these colonies foraged less under the warmer chamber setting. The trial-to-trial and session-to-session spread inside a colony feeds into the colony means but is not counted as replication of the manipulation; with 10 colonies from 3 collection sites, site effects are not separable from colony identity in this design.

Each colony contributes eight rows (2 conditions x 2 sessions x 2 trials), so rows within a colony are repeated measurements of the same nest and are correlated: they describe how precisely that colony's foraging rate was measured, not how many colonies responded to warming. The four trials of a colony within a condition should therefore be averaged into a single value per colony per condition, leaving ten independent paired observations, one per colony, for any comparison of the two chamber settings. There are 80 rows in total.

evidence.description: The workflow collapses the repeated trial rows to a single mean per colony per condition before any inferential test, so each independent unit (colony_id) enters the test exactly once per condition.
evidence.observed_value: one averaged value per (colony, condition) cell; error raised if trial counts differ

evidence.description: The paired t-test is run on the colony-level arrays (10 values per condition), not on the 80 trial rows, and the degrees of freedom are computed from the number of colonies.

evidence.description: The reported test statistics reflect the colony-level analysis: df = 9 matches 10 colonies minus 1 (a row-level analysis of 80 rows would give df = 79 and a much smaller SE), and the selected result states n = 10 colonies. Independent recomputation from the CSV reproduces mean difference -2.900, SD 1.148, SE 0.363, and t = -7.99 exactly.

source_refs.quoted_text: The 4 trials a colony contributes within a condition are repeated measurements of the same colony; they replicate the measurement, not the warming manipulation. Every colony is therefore collapsed to one ambient mean and one warmed mean before any test is run, and the inferential comparison uses the 10 colony-level differences - one analyzed observation per independent unit.

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I tried to show the issue was present by checking whether the reported statistics could only arise from a row-level (per-trial) analysis. I recomputed everything from data/input.csv by hand: the ten colony means per condition match the report's table exactly (e.g., C01 ambient 22.40, C07 difference -0.70, C10 ambient 26.30); the ten differences sum to -29.0 giving mean -2.900; squared deviations sum to 11.86 giving SD sqrt(11.86/9) = 1.148 and SE 1.148/sqrt(10) = 0.363; t = -2.900/0.363 = -7.99 with df = 9. A per-trial paired analysis would instead have df = 39 (40 trial pairs) or df = 79 and a deflated SE; the reported df = 9 and SE 0.363 are inconsistent with any row-level pooling and consistent only with one observation per colony. I also traced the code path: read_trials groups values by (colony, condition), collapse_to_colony_means averages them, and only the length-10 arrays reach stats.ttest_rel. I found no code path by which individual trial rows enter the test.
